comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C47, C48, C49. Both evaluations find the pulse-chase assay data supporting that the isolated HECT domain is insufficient for substrate ubiquitination while WW3-HECT is competent. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED; peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of the 'detailed biochemistry' without specific critique.

Perfect agreement on claims C120-C123 regarding generality across substrates and NEDD4-family E3s. Both find the data supportive. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED; peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED but request clarification about substrate-specific differences in diubiquitin formation assays.

Strong agreement on claims C127-C137, C140 regarding substrate selection and spatial constraints. Both evaluations find the substrate selection assays validate the structural model's predictions about lysine positioning. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED; peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED and note consistency between structural predictions and biochemical data.

Significant disagreement on structural claims C62-C77, C124-C126, C144. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on electron density maps and correlation with mutagenesis. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, expressing serious concern that the crosslinking approach may stabilize 'an usually underpopulated conformation' and stating 'the authors have a significant burden of proof.'

Agreement on claims C52-C55 regarding alanine scan demonstrating distinct surfaces for E2-to-E3 transfer versus ligation. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the structural interpretation; peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'convincing' but request clarification about whether some mutations affect C-lobe versus MBP fusion interactions.

Strong agreement on claims C82-C88 (particularly C85-C87) regarding N-lobe/C-lobe interface importance. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the specificity of ligation defects; peer reviewers highlight the 'rescue of mutants in the C-lobe through mutation of opposing residues in the N-lobe' as strong validation.

Agreement on claims C79-C81 regarding Arg74 and Glu502 mutations. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites quantitative kinetic data; peer reviewers note the R501A/E502A experiment 'similarly addresses the validity of this interface' and recommend integration into main text.

Agreement on claims C89-C97 (particularly C93-C95) regarding aromatic anchor rescue experiments. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the 43-fold rescue and selectivity; peer reviewers view the complementary mutagenesis as strong validation of the N-lobe/C-lobe interface.

Agreement on claims C66-C70 regarding ubiquitin-HECT interface mutations. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mutations at conserved interface impair activity while Ile44 mutations do not; peer reviewers do not specifically critique these claims but they are part of the mutagenesis data validating the structural model.

Disagreement on claims C103-C109, C115-C117 regarding Rosetta modeling. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveat that modeling is computational; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating the detailed discussion is 'more appropriate for a high-resolution crystal structure rather than modeling based on a moderate-resolution structure containing a chemical cross-linker.'

Agreement on claims C112-C114, C119 regarding 491-495 loop importance. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the mechanism remains speculative; peer reviewers do not specifically comment but these claims are part of the 'convincing' alanine scanning data.

Partial overlap on claims C3-C7 regarding the distinct catalytic architecture. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED based on crystal structure showing ~130° rotation; peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for the two-state model but emphasize need for additional validation given crosslinking concerns.

Agreement on claims C141-C147, C160-C161 regarding the integrated model and three-way anchored architecture. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the ~130° rotation and reduced flexibility; peer reviewers confirm the model is supported by 'detailed biochemistry' but require additional validation of the structural approach.

Agreement on summary claims C160-C161 regarding lysine prioritization and conservation across NEDD4-family E3s. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites crystal structure, alanine scan, and substrate selection assays; peer reviewers acknowledge the model is supported by structural and biochemical data.

OpenEval evaluates background claims C1, C2, C8, C9, C11-C14 about the two-step HECT mechanism as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are established knowledge rather than novel findings.

OpenEval rates claims C98-C102 about C-terminus role as UNCERTAIN due to conflicting data (deletion impairs but substitutions do not). No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
OpenEval evaluates claims C148-C154 comparing HECT and RING E3 mechanisms as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this comparative mechanistic discussion.

OpenEval rates claims C162-C166 about HECT domain reloading and polyubiquitination mechanisms as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative inferences lacking direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
